title: Make the ledger honest + precise
summary: Two upgrades that turn a green checkmark from 'a list was submitted' into 'code was actually inspected'. (1) Evidence-weighted coverage: every checked item now carries how it was verified (detector/code-read/test vs reasoned/assumed), and the worker + UI report verified/total alongside matched/total. (2) Context-aware scanner precision: the three noisiest detectors stop firing on esc()-wrapped HTML, noindex pages, and already-sourced stats, and every finding is tagged high-confidence vs needs-review. Shipped to production and verified end-to-end.

bugfixes: XSS-INNERHTML no longer flags esc()-wrapped / numeric / literal interpolations
SEO-NO-OG/DESC no longer flag pages marked noindex
CLAIM-UNSOURCED-STAT no longer flags a stat that carries an adjacent citation
findings: The old green tick certified a submitted list, not an audit — it could not tell code-read from title-listed.
My own earlier '73 already-escaped' critique was an overstatement: only ~6 are purely safe to drop; the real fix is the confidence split, not mass deletion.
Removing a name-based 'loop counter is safe' shortcut prevented a real false negative (img src="${d}" where d is photo data).
insights: Precision beats recall for a shared detector: when 99% is noise, a real finding gets pattern-dismissed with the rest.
Verify the critic — including yourself: measuring the claimed 73 esc-wrapped strings corrected the plan before it shipped.
